text: {"observations":"Tonal harmonics glide downward from 0-2 s (motor spinning down) over broadband noise, then near-silence from ~2.8-4.6 s. At ~4.6 s there is an abrupt broadband onset with harmonics sweeping up within ~0.3 s to steady lines (~1, 2, 4, 6.2 kHz) held until ~7.4 s, then gliding down again. Fast motor spin-up/spin-down with strong airflow-like broadband noise fits a vacuum cleaner being switched on and off (C). It rules out frying (A, no steady tonal harmonics expected), typing (D, would be sparse clicks), and makes a washing machine (B, slower spin changes, lower-frequency rumble) less likely.","answer":"C"}
